thread:
Matt R: Quick heads-up — I’m seeing a clear spike in token-level p95 on /generate after last runtime patch. p50 fine, but p95 +60ms.
Lina C: hmm, did the kernel-selection heuristic change in that deploy?
Matt R: yes — we switched to the heuristic that prefers int8 kernels for matmul when seq_len < 512. It looked safe in perf tests.
Yoav: perf-bot just triggered an alert: `route:/generate token_latency_p95 > 250ms` at 1767893234 :eyes:
perf-bot: alert: route=/generate, p95_token_latency=272ms, baseline_p95=210ms, regression=29%
Dan S: can we get a breakdown by token stage? tokenization / kv-lookup / matmul / postproc?
Amira: pulled a quick token-level breakdown from the tracing dashboard:
```
token_stage_latency_ms{stage="tokenize"} => p95=3.2
token_stage_latency_ms{stage="kv_cache_lookup"} => p95=6.5, hit_rate=78%
token_stage_latency_ms{stage="matmul"} => p95=210.1
token_stage_latency_ms{stage="postproc"} => p95=4.0
```
Lina C: matmul dominating. But batch sizes look smaller than usual — scheduler cut earlier. Batch hist: p50=4, p90=8, p99=16; before patch p50=8, p90=16.
Matt R: interesting — so smaller batches + int8 kernel for short seq might be triggering worse kernel routing conditions?
Yoav: I profiled kernel selection logs for a sample:
```
[1767893248] model=gptx-7b seq=128 batch=4 chosen_kernel=f32_matmul reason=latency_estimate
[1767893249] model=gptx-7b seq=128 batch=4 chosen_kernel=int8_matmul reason=quant_fallback
[1767893250] model=gptx-7b seq=128 batch=8 chosen_kernel=int8_matmul reason=quant_fallback
```
Shows flip-flopping for same seq/batch patterns.
Dan S: flip-flop could cause cache misses for compiled kernels, more JIT overhead and kernel-switching latency.
Amira: KV cache hit rate dropped from 85% -> 78% in same window, probably because of changed batching / prefix grouping. More cold starts.
Lina C: action: revert kernel-selection heuristic to v1 for canary, and add a guard that forces kernel stability if batch_size < 8.
Matt R: +1. Also want a new dashboard panel: per-route kernel-selected histogram (counts of f32/int8/other) over last 30m, and a metric for kernel-switches_per_min.
Yoav: wrote a PromQL snippet we can use for kernel-switch rate: `sum(rate(kernel_switches_total[1m])) by (model,route)` — should show scheduler churn.
perf-bot: deploy-bot started canary deploy 1767893300 for runtime rollback v1-heuristic :rocket:
deploy-bot: canary nodes=5, traffic=5%
Dan S: also add a panel that overlays batch_size_histogram with queue_wait_p50/p95 to capture scheduler efficiency. Current queue_wait_p95 climbed from 14ms -> 42ms.
Amira: attaching sample hist numbers from the sampling run: batch_size_histogram buckets: {1:120k,2:80k,4:40k,8:10k,16:2k}, queue_wait_ms_p95=42, scheduler_efficiency=0.73
Lina C: good call. I'll add alerts: if kernel_switches_per_min > 10 AND queue_wait_p95 > 30ms trigger SEV2.
Matt R: once canary is up, let's run a profiling suite focused on these axes: per-route token-stage latency, kernel-switch rate, batch-size distribution, kv_cache_hit_by_prefix_length.
Yoav: noted. I'll also instrument per-route cost metric so we can correlate unit-cost with latency regressions.
Amira: leaving a short runbook note: when you see p95 regressions but p50 stable, check (1) kernel selection churn, (2) batch size distribution, (3) KV cache hit rate, (4) compiled-kernel cache churn.
Matt R: thanks team. Lina — can you post the canary results in this thread? :thumbsup:
Lina C: will do. starting monitoring now, ping me if you see anything odd.
perf-bot: canary results after 5m: p95_token_latency(route=/generate) -> reverted to 215ms (back near baseline). kernel_switches_per_min dropped from 18->3.
Matt R: perfect — closing the loop. We'll keep the new dashboard tiles and the kernel-stability guard for next ship.
Yoav: filed follow-up ticket: INF-7212 "Dashboard: kernel-selection heatmap + kernel-switch metric"
Matt R: nice. closing thread.
